newsitem.title: DOMINICAN REPUBLIC: Dominican government defends boost in salaries.
newsitem.headline: Dominican government defends boost in salaries.

text.p: Dominican President Leonel Fernandez said on Wednesday he was planning "a substantial" increase in government workers' salaries in 1997 after criticism of up to 2,000 percent increases in the pay of top government officials.

Opposition members of Congress have objected to the plan to raise top officials' pay because it excluded other public servants and have pushed for a plan to increase the salaries of other officials, including raising their own salaries from $1,200 to $5,000 a month.
Fernandez's salary was increased to $7,500 a month from $250. The salaries of the vice president, cabinet secretaries and sub-secretaries and director generals also were lifted.

The president on Wednesday took personal responsibility for the raises and said the salaries of other government officials could not be increased because the Dominican treasury lacked sufficient funds.
But he said he was planning "a substantial" general increase in the salaries of government workers beginning in 1997, after a reform of the nation's tax system.
Fernandez had called for higher government salaries when he was elected last summer, saying they would help fight public corruption by making illegal payments less attractive.
